title: A diode nanocavity for fast, efficient and tunable emission of highly entangled photon pairs and Fourier-transform-limited single photons
authors: Ievgen Brytavskyi, Thomas Oberleitner, Christian Weidinger, Maximilian Aigner, Gabriel Undeutsch, Tobias Steindl, Johannes Reindl, Ailton Garcia, Melina Peter, Christian Schimpf, Santanu Manna, Michele B. Rota, Quirin Buchinger, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Rinaldo Trotta, Tobias M. Krieger, Eva Schöll, Armando Rastelli
abstract: Deterministic sources of entangled photon pairs and indistinguishable photons are expected to play a key role in photonic quantum technologies. Semiconductor quantum dots are promising candidates due to their on-demand emission and compatibility with nanophotonic structures. However, current implementations face trade-offs between extraction efficiency, Purcell enhancement, as well as charge noise that causes blinking and degrades indistinguishability. Here we demonstrate a tunable nano-optoelectronic device based on a quantum dot embedded in a p-i-n diode circular-Bragg-grating-resonator and featuring extraction efficiencies up to 0.55(6) and Purcell-factor of $\sim$8. The device generates wavelength-tunable entangled photon pairs with suppressed blinking and raw (corrected) concurrence > 0.89 (0.91) over a range of 1.6 nm. The very same source also emits single, nearly Fourier-limited and highly indistinguishable photons with raw (corrected) $\mathcal{V}_{\text{HOM}}$ = 0.951(4) (0.988(6)). These results demonstrate a viable platform for semiconductor quantum photonics.
summary: The paper reports the successful realization of a tunable, high-performance solid-state source for entangled and single photons using a novel diode nanocavity structure. By combining a quantum dot with a p-i-n diode and a Bragg grating resonator, the authors overcome limitations in efficiency and stability, demonstrating near-unity indistinguishability and high entanglement fidelity across a measurable spectral range.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a reliable, efficient, and tunable solid-state platform for generating highly entangled photon pairs and indistinguishable single photons.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a novel diode nanocavity structure that achieves high entanglement fidelity ($F > 0.94$) and near-unity single-photon indistinguishability ($V_{HOM} \approx 0.95$), while maintaining tunability over 1.6 nm.
method: The experiment utilizes a quantum dot embedded in a p-i-n diode circular-Bragg-grating-resonator, characterized by electrical measurements (I-V curves) and optical characterization of photon pairs and single photons.
model_or_system: The physical system is a semiconductor quantum dot integrated into a diode structure coupled to a circular-Bragg-grating resonator. This architecture allows for deterministic charge control via the diode, enhancing emission efficiency and suppressing blinking effects.
key_observables: Concurrence ($C$), entanglement fidelity ($F_{|\Phi^+angle}$), single-photon indistinguishability ($\mathcal{V}_{	ext{HOM}}$), extraction efficiency ($\eta_{	ext{ext}}$), and Purcell factor ($F_P$).
important_parameters: Tunable wavelength range of 1.6 nm, high raw concurrence (>0.89) and fidelity (>0.94), and a maximum Purcell factor of $\sim$8.
main_assumptions: The measurements are performed at low temperatures (4 K), and the device performance is optimized based on theoretical FDTD simulations using specific geometric parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental workflow, the physical structure (SEM image), and comparisons between simulated and measured optical properties like Purcell factor and extraction efficiency spectra.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard experimental structure: introduction establishing the need for solid-state sources; detailed description of the novel diode-CBR device fabrication and characterization; presentation of results showing high-quality entangled pairs and single photons across a tunable range; and concluding remarks on its viability.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses key challenges in quantum optics by integrating electrical control (diode) with strong optical enhancement (nanocavity) to create robust sources for photonic quantum information processing.
